lines.meet: I'm Pieter, and I'll take the hits, because I'm the one wearing the armour. Now check your straps before we go anywhere.
lines.meet_neighbour: Northern Tanaris, ja, the dig sites. I'm Pieter, with the clipboard, and I've checked your straps from a distance.
lines.ask_home: Where were you raised, then? It's good to know who I'm standing in front of.
lines.ask_work: What line of work were you in? Tell me before I see how you handle a harness.
lines.answer_home: Pretoria, born and raised, then twenty-eight years in Rotterdam. My wife's Dutch.
lines.answer_work: Port safety officer, twenty-eight years. Clipboard, hard hat, and the most tedious man on the dock, ja.
lines.chat_food: A braai on a Sunday, boerewors and pap, with a cold beer. And my wife's stamppot, which I'll defend to the death.
lines.chat_sleep: Seven hours, ja, after a safety check of the tent. You'd be amazed what crawls in.
lines.chat_missing: Rugby on a Saturday, with my girls shouting at the ref louder than me. They learned it from me.
lines.chat_here: A world with monsters in it needs a safety man more than a port does. I took to this place straight away, and I'm a bit ashamed of that.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd make a good safety officer, {name}. Nobody'd notice you until it mattered.
lines.tease_talker: Lekker, {name}, you never stop talking. At least I always know where you are.
lines.tease_careful: Harness, then harness again, {name}. Ja, you're my favourite person on this dig.
lines.tease_bold: Jislaaik, {name}, you'd walk under a crane without looking up. I've filled in forms about people like you.
lines.tease_any: Your straps are a disgrace, {name}, every morning. I check them anyway, and I always will.
lines.tease_back: Ha, lekker, {name}, that one got through my guard.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ja, fair enough, {name}. Anneke would tell you the same.
lines.apologise: I was rude there, ja, and I'm sorry for it. I'm gruff, but I'm not usually rude.
lines.double_down: Nee, it stands. A safety man doesn't take back a warning.
lines.needle_quiet: A loose strap nobody reports is how small things become funerals. Say what you see.
lines.needle_talker: Less talking, more checking, please. The pit doesn't care how interesting you are.
lines.needle_careful: Enough checking, ja. Now trust the harness and go.
lines.needle_bold: You're a man in a hurry, and I've buried men in a hurry. You need to slow down.
lines.needle_any: You keep saying accidents happen. They don't happen, they're caused, and you cause them.
lines.bite_back: Twenty-eight years of nobody dying on my dock. Lecture me when you've done the same.
lines.hurt: Ja, okay, that one hit. I'll go and check some straps for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, I've been shouted at by thousands of men in a hurry. You'll have to queue.
lines.confide: {name}, I've pulled nine men out of those pits in three years. I keep the number because somebody should. I don't talk about the ones I didn't.
lines.listen: Ja, {name}, I'm listening. That stays off the clipboard.
lines.look_out: Get behind the armour, {name}, ja? That's arithmetic, not courage.
lines.accept: Ja, {name}, your plan. Check your straps first, mind.
lines.deflect: A dent, {name}, that's what the armour's for. Check the others.
lines.check_in: Ja, {name}, where's the damage? Tell me straight, I've filled in a lot of forms.
lines.blame: Somebody didn't check before they went in, ja. That's how it always starts.
lines.thank: The armour wasn't enough there, and you were. Dankie, thank you.
lines.brush_off: Ag, it's nothing, ja. Sit, and let me check your straps while you're down.
lines.worry: Jislaaik, {name}, that was close. Sit down and don't move till I've looked.
lines.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, ja. I'll keep it inspected.
lines.hand_fine: Ja, you keep it, it's better on you. I've got my father's knife.
lines.hand_sulk: There's a procedure, ja, and it starts with asking, and nobody asked.
lines.turn_friendly: You check your straps without being told now, {name}. That's a friend, as far as I'm concerned.
lines.turn_friends: I'd trust you to rig my harness, {name}. I've never said that to anybody but my father.
lines.turn_grating: We don't see eye to eye, ja. I'll keep you safe anyway, that's the job.
lines.turn_rivals: The armour's on me, so I take the hits in front of you. Arithmetic, not friendship.
lines.make_up: Ag, {name}, this nonsense has gone on long enough. Let's start again, ja?
lines.defend: Nee, that's wrong, and I was watching. Back off from {name}.
lines.friend_left: Nobody's here to tease about their straps since {name} went home.
lines.friend_back: Straps first, {name}, then we talk. Welcome back, ja.
lines.common_parent: Two girls, Lotte and Sanne, grown now, in Rotterdam. They shout at the rugby louder than me.
lines.common_docks: Twenty-eight years on the docks at Rotterdam. Anybody who's worked a port knows the danger's always the thing nobody's watching.
